text:
sara_sales: quick heads-up — prospect (FinWave) wants a POC. must prove a stable, auditable egress IP for outbound calls to their onprem API and they want mTLS termination on their side. they asked: PrivateLink vs peering which keeps src IP, and what pricing delta for static egress. any obvious blockers?

josh_solutions: short answer: PrivateLink = interface endpoints into customer VPC; traffic originates from our infra so client src IP won't be preserved. peering/transit can preserve, but more ops on both sides. pricing: PrivateLink usually has endpoint-hour + data transfer; peering/transit is mainly data transfer and infra config.

maria_netops: clarifying network bits — if we do PrivateLink (interface endpoint), our connector egress will be SNATed by their endpoint unless they add proxy translation rules. to preserve source IP you need a routed path where packets come from customer's side or a proxy that forwards original IP in headers (we support X-Forwarded-For). also note mutual TLS: if they terminate mTLS, we'll need to deliver plain TLS from our side to their proxy or terminate mutually at their edge.

maria_netops: firewall snippet they can use on their edge (we asked for the minimal allowlist):
```
Allow outbound to our egress IPs: 203.0.113.45/32, 203.0.113.46/32
Ports: 443 (TCP) for API; optionally 123/udp for NTP sync if they require timestamping.
SNI: allow TLS SNI for *.redwood.example
```

ali_infra: pricing/ops note — to guarantee a stable public egress IP in hosted mode we can: 1) reserve a small NAT pool on Dedicated; 2) offer a fixed egress via our egress-proxy (adds monthly infra fee). both have different SLAs. estimate: reserved egress IPs add ~$2k/month for a small POC (ballpark), egress-proxy increases bandwidth cost by ~10%. I'll confirm precise quote.

sara_sales: great — buyer also sent a security questionnaire asking for a data-flow diagram and attack surface for PrivateLink vs peering. what level of detail do they expect?

compliance_bot: security checklist reminder — include: data residency, audit logs retention (we keep request logs for 90 days by default), key management (KMS used on private deployments), and network diagram per env. I'll attach standard template if you want.

josh_solutions: suggested POC plan (2-week):
1) week 0: exchange IPs and certs, run basic connectivity test (https://curl -> status 200)
2) week 1: run PrivateLink quickproof (fastest path, lower infra ops) — confirm if X-Forwarded-For acceptable
3) week 2: if they insist on preserved src ip, shift to routed peering/transit test and run traffic capture and firewall validation
add a canary dataset and perf SLA check (latency and error budget).

maria_netops: ops reminders: we need their CIDR block for route table entries, and a list of FW admins for the handoff window. also ask if they expect MTU tweaks for GRE/IPSec.

sara_sales: ok i'll send them two asks: certificate exchange + preferred model (PrivateLink test first). ali, can you confirm cost delta by EOD? maria, can you draft the minimal network diagram for the sec questionnaire? i'll book a 30m POC kickoff for tues 10am PT. :calendar:

ali_infra: will confirm numbers by EOD.

maria_netops: will drop the diagram (png + short notes) into the vendor doc bucket and ping you here when done.

sara_sales: thanks team — will update customer and move to formal SOW once they pick path. :thumbsup:
